title: 1987 AHSME Problem 11
statement: Let \(c\) be a constant. The simultaneous equations \[ \begin{aligned} x-y&=2,\\ cx+y&=3. \end{aligned} \] have a solution \((x,y)\) inside Quadrant I if and only if

solutions.text:
Solving the system gives \[ x=\frac5{c+1},\qquad y=\frac{3-2c}{c+1}. \] The condition \(x\gt0\) requires \(c\gt-1.\) With this positive denominator, \(y\gt0\) is equivalent to \(c\lt\frac{3}{2}.\) Hence \(-1\lt c\lt\frac{3}{2}.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Solve the two equations for \(x\) and \(y\) in terms of \(c\)
Quadrant I requires both coordinates to be strictly positive
